batches.one_line_summary: customers (CUSTOMER_MASTER + 8337 embedded ENTITY_ATTR_VALUE rows) loaded to mmp_rt_billing.customers with pymongo backend; fixture PASS and one live PASS (25001 docs, 33338 Tier-3 checks, 0 findings), but result.json merge_eligible=false because the harness structurally warns on any child_where-scoped embed — needs an orchestrator/human ruling, not a code fix; PR #1714 updated (rebased onto run tip, reused prior branch).
skill_feedback: Harness (mongo-recon-harness/harness/recon/report.py:64) sets merge_eligible=false whenever any warning exists, and tiers.py:345-349 always emits 'embed <path>: scoped by a where-predicate; extra target elements not checked' for embeds with child_where/target_where. So a mapping with a scoped embed (customers.attributes, ENTITY_TYPE='CUSTOMER') can never be merge_eligible even with live PASS; the profile/playbook does not document this. Needs a harness rule (e.g. treat the warning as informational when Tier 1 embed cardinality matches and Tier 3 is full_diff) or a human decision row.
Oracle SUM over zero non-NULL values returns NULL; ported reports.BALANCES_SQL with a $cond non-null counter so the mongo path returns None instead of 0.
*_YN columns are stored as bool per mapping; facade parity needs 'Y'/'N' rendering on read (derived, not in profile).

Shared helper common.load_embedded_collection writes attributes: [] for roots with no child rows (rather than omitting the field); harness accepts it, but the profile does not state which is canonical.

batches.one_line_summary: invoice_batch landed on Atlas (18750 invoice_headers with 149963 embedded lines, 37 invoice_line_orphans) and live recon on the migration cluster PASSED all 3 tiers (168750 keyed checks, idempotent re-load), but result.json merge_eligible=false because the harness zeroes eligibility on the unavoidable 'scoped embed: extra target elements not checked' warning from the mapping's child_where; PR #1723 open, needs a harness/mapping decision from the orchestrator, not a code fix.
skill_feedback: Harness (mongo-recon-harness 0.3.2): report.py:64 sets merge_eligible only when `warnings` is empty, and tiers.py:337-349 always emits 'embed ...: scoped by a where-predicate; extra target elements not checked' whenever an embed has child_where or target_where. Any mapping that scopes an embed to exclude orphan child rows (the only way for Tier 1 to pass when orphans exist) therefore can never be merge-eligible, even with a live PASS on the migration cluster. In full-diff mode the `seen` key set per parent is complete, so extras could be graded for scoped embeds; either grade them or do not count this warning against merge_eligible. The orchestrator's grading-only amendment (target_where '{}' added to unblock the earlier attempt) unblocked the run but still trips this warning.

Profile oracle.md has no rule for TO_CHAR(SUM(x), 'FM999999999999990.00') semantics (SUM over all-NULL group -> NULL -> None; otherwise a plain 2-dp decimal string); derived in invoice_batch.fm_money.

Profile has no rule for Oracle implicit NUMBER-vs-VARCHAR2 comparison in outer joins (`codes.code_val (+) = invoice_header.status_cd`); mapped as an int-to-int $lookup because wave-0 stored codeVal as int.
Profile has no rule for ORDER BY collation: Oracle NLS_SORT=BINARY matched by MongoDB default (binary) sort; a non-binary NLS_SORT would need a collation on the aggregate.

Wave-0 common.py counted orphan child rows but never wrote them; the orphan-sibling-collection pattern (single child scan, parentless rows to a sink with orphan:true) had to be added as `orphan_sink` in load_embedded_collection.

findings: Batch w1-b03 re-ran green in live mode against the migration cluster for all three units (subscriptions_rating, invoicing, dunning) with merge_eligible=true in each result.json, so the batch is PASS and PR #1718 is eligible for the workflow to merge.

Every past-the-gate probe (counts, duplicate keys, null and missing rates, embed array lengths and orphans, boundary aggregates, BSON types, indexes versus index_plan, cluster inventory) and every cross-unit reference check returned zero discrepancies against Oracle.

All seven replayed app-level parity queries (paged usage list, usage sum by tenant, credit remaining by tenant, invoices by status, active subscriptions by plan, dunning list, rating overage count) return identical results from Oracle and from the loaded Mongo collections.

Observation, not a defect: the ported dunning.py updates tenants.statusCd and subscriptions at runtime just as the PL/SQL does, so the wave-0 tenants collection is a runtime write target of this unit even though it is not a loader write target.
